slides.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for humanoid robots to coordinate force and motion during contact-rich tasks, offering insights relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: FLoRe enables force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation by learning from robot-free demonstrations with contact wrench data.
card.key_idea: Combines a force-reactive diffusion policy with a hybrid compliance whole-body controller that tracks per-hand force commands while maintaining balance.
card.evaluation: Tested on Unitree G1 in three contact-rich tasks; achieved 80% success vs 26.7% for position-only baselines, with ~1N force tracking error in simulation.
card.limitation: Force tracking accuracy degrades for lateral/downward commands, and the system requires specific handheld grippers with F/T sensors for data collection.

slides.title: PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper introduces PhysLadder, a benchmark evaluating contact-rich manipulation capabilities, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's AR/VR human-in-the-loop testbed for assessing physical interaction and coordination.

card.one_liner: PhysLadder benchmarks GPT-6 Astra on 16 contact-rich tasks, showing zero L3 success in both sim and real.
card.key_idea: Hierarchical benchmark organizing 16 tasks by contact configuration and force regulation, with physically and visually matched sim-real environments.
card.evaluation: Zero-shot GPT-6 Astra on 16 tasks (3 trials each); success drops from 80% (L1) to 0% (L3) in real world, with consistent sim trends.
card.limitation: Small sample size (3 trials/task) and reliance on qualitative matching may limit statistical robustness and generalizability to other models.

slides.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that preserves contact force targets when retargeting human demonstrations to robots, significantly improving task success rates compared to kinematic-only methods.

card.one_liner: CARD retargets human demos to robots by preserving contact force targets, enabling object-free dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Optimizes robot configurations to align fingertip pads with human contact force targets (location, direction, magnitude) without object models or simulators.
card.evaluation: Tested on video, glove, and motion capture data plus GRAB; achieves 43-78% contact fidelity vs <10% for kinematic baselines.
card.limitation: Open-loop replay cannot recover from large object displacements; retargeting quality is bounded by input demonstration fidelity.

slides.title: Tokens of Motion: Primitive Motion Learning for Human-Humanoid Skill Transfer
slides.highlight: The paper introduces Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL), a framework that leverages failure trajectories to guide Vision-Language-Action policies, enhancing robustness in robotic manipulation. This approach is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction by offering a method to improve the reliability of skill transfer and execution in complex environments.

card.one_liner: M-PACT transfers human skills to humanoids by learning reusable motion primitives from video, requiring minimal robot data.
card.key_idea: Factorizes motion into embodiment-agnostic primitives via self-supervised segmentation and tokenization, adapting only a lightweight decoder for new robots.
card.evaluation: Tested on EgoDex, HoloAssist, and HumanoidEveryday; demonstrates strong reconstruction and transfer with ~100 robot demos, validated on real humanoids.
card.limitation: Contextual primitive prediction accuracy remains low, and aperture reconstruction struggles when motion variations are limited.

slides.title: DEX-PHD: A Dexterous Portable Handheld Device for Multimodal Data Collection
slides.highlight: This work introduces a portable handheld device for collecting multimodal data on dexterous manipulation, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on non-data-hungry multimodal social perception by demonstrating efficient, untethered data acquisition methods.

card.one_liner: DEX-PHD is a portable handheld device integrating a dexterous robot hand for synchronized multimodal data collection.
card.key_idea: Integrates a dexterous robot hand with continuous per-finger control and onboard logging of joint states, fingertip forces, and wrist-camera video.
card.evaluation: Tested on contact-rich tasks (peg-in-hole, grasping, drilling) via open-loop replay on a humanoid robot, analyzing joint tracking and contact correlations.
card.limitation: Open-loop replay causes contact timing and force profile variations due to object pose misalignment and whole-body motion errors.

slides.title: The Language of Deformation: Semantic Failure Analysis as a Prerequisite for Dexterous Manipulation of Deformable Objects
slides.tldr: SEMANTIC FAILURE ANALYSIS FOR DEFORMABLE OBJECTS
slides.highlight: This work argues that semantic failure analysis is essential for advancing dexterous manipulation of deformable objects, addressing complex failure modes like buckling and tearing that rigid-object methods overlook.

card.one_liner: Proposes semantic failure analysis as a prerequisite for robust robotic manipulation of deformable objects.
card.key_idea: Formalizes Semantic Failure Analysis (SFA-DOM) to classify failure modes like buckling or tearing from tactile data and map them to corrective strategies.
card.evaluation: Proof-of-concept experiments with a Hall-effect sensor on balloon, clay, paper, and filament demonstrate distinct tactile signatures for various failure modes.
card.limitation: Requires high-resolution, contact-proximal tactile sensing and low-inertia force actuation, which are hardware bottlenecks in current industrial manipulators.

slides.title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how egocentric human demonstrations can be effectively transferred to humanoid robots via a specialized VLA training pipeline, addressing embodiment gaps relevant to embodied learning in RwB.

card.one_liner: HuGe scales humanoid VLAs using 2,000+ hours of egocentric data and a three-stage training pipeline.
card.key_idea: Three-stage pipeline pre-trains on egocentric data with pseudo-proprioception, adapts to robots, and fine-tunes with visual arm replacement.
card.evaluation: SOTA on HumanoidArena simulation and improved real-world Unitree G1 pick-and-drop success via egocentric data augmentation.
card.limitation: Real-world grasping failures due to balance instability from heavy dexterous hands; limited fine-grained manipulation performance.

slides.title: EXE: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Pretraining via Factorized Latent Actions for VLA Models
slides.tldr: FACTORIZED LATENT ACTIONS FOR CROSS-EMBODIMENT TRANSFER
slides.highlight: This work addresses the embodiment gap in learning manipulation skills from egocentric human videos by factorizing latent actions into shared manipulation priors and embodiment-specific signals. This approach aligns with MOSAIC's goal of estimating human proficiency and transferring skills to AI agents by isolating transferable procedural knowledge from human-specific kinematics.

card.one_liner: EXE pretrains VLAs on egocentric human video by factorizing actions into shared positional and embodiment-specific latent spaces.
card.key_idea: Factorizes actions into shared positional and private kinematic subspaces, aligning shared codes via contrastive learning and language-guided distillation.
card.evaluation: Tested on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa GR1, and real-world tasks; outperforms baselines without robot pretraining, with ablations confirming component efficacy.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate MANO hand-pose extraction from video and assumes 3D position is the primary transferable manipulation signal.
